diagnosis: High-grade B-cell lymphoma with MYC and BCL2 rearrangements (double-hit lymphoma; WHO-HAEM5 name DLBCL/HGBL-MYC/BCL2), germinal-center B-cell (GCB) phenotype by the Hans algorithm (CD10+, BCL6+, MUM1-). The original 2026-09-12 sign-out of DLBCL, NOS is superseded by the 2026-09-19 FISH addendum (IGH::MYC and IGH::BCL2 fusions; BCL6 not rearranged). CD23-, CD30- and the cervical nodal biopsy site argue against primary mediastinal B-cell lymphoma. The EHR problem list still reads DLBCL and should be updated.
stage: Lugano (Ann Arbor) stage II bulky (IIA-X): FDG-avid right cervical nodes and a 12.0 cm anterior mediastinal mass, all above the diaphragm. No B symptoms. No extranodal, splenic, osseous, marrow, testicular or CNS involvement on PET-CT. A 12 cm mass is bulky, so this is managed as advanced-stage disease rather than limited-stage disease.
biology: Double-hit: FISH shows MYC rearrangement (IGH::MYC, t(8;14)) and BCL2 rearrangement (IGH::BCL2, t(14;18)); BCL6 is not rearranged, so it is not triple-hit. It is also double-expressor by IHC (MYC 80%, BCL2 90%), but the FISH-defined double-hit status is the key classification and drives treatment. Ki-67 about 95%, starry-sky pattern. GCB cell of origin by Hans.
prognosis: IPI 1 (low by score): only LDH is above normal (740 rising to 812 U/L, about 3.6x ULN); age 54, ECOG 1, stage II and no extranodal sites score 0. Age-adjusted IPI 1 and CNS-IPI 1. These scores underestimate the risk: the MYC and BCL2 rearrangements (double-hit biology) dominate prognosis, with poorer outcomes after standard therapy and a higher risk of CNS relapse.
first_line_treatment: The 2026-09-14 plan of R-CHOP x6 starting 2026-09-22 was written before the FISH addendum and is outdated: cancel it. Recommend curative-intent DA-EPOCH-R (dose-adjusted etoposide, prednisone, vincristine, cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin, rituximab) for 6 cycles, or enrollment in a clinical trial for MYC/BCL2-rearranged lymphoma if one is available; R-hyper-CVAD/MA or R-CODOX-M/R-IVAC are acceptable intensive alternatives at experienced centers. R-CHOP alone is not preferred for rearrangement-defined double-hit lymphoma. Start promptly (within about 1 week) given rapid growth and SVC compression. Consolidative involved-site radiotherapy (ISRT) to the bulky mediastinal site should be decided at multidisciplinary review, particularly for residual PET-positive disease at the end of treatment.
cns_risk: Double-hit biology carries a high risk of CNS involvement and relapse regardless of the CNS-IPI of 1 (no kidney, adrenal or other high-risk extranodal sites). Before cycle 1: contrast-enhanced MRI brain and lumbar puncture with CSF cytology and flow cytometry. CNS prophylaxis should be given: intrathecal methotrexate is commonly given with DA-EPOCH-R per protocol, and systemic high-dose methotrexate (for example 2 cycles at 3 g/m2 or more) is an alternative; renal function is normal (creatinine 0.9), so high-dose methotrexate is feasible if chosen. If MRI or CSF shows CNS disease, the plan changes to a CNS-directed regimen.
response_assessment: Interim FDG PET-CT after cycles 2-4 (commonly after cycle 2 or 4 of DA-EPOCH-R) to confirm response; progression should prompt re-biopsy and a change of therapy, otherwise complete all 6 cycles. End-of-treatment FDG PET-CT 6-8 weeks after cycle 6 (and before any radiotherapy), read with Lugano 2014 criteria and the Deauville 5-point scale; Deauville 1-3 is a complete metabolic response. Residual Deauville 4-5 uptake in the mediastinum should be biopsied if it would change management, or treated with ISRT after multidisciplinary review.
pretreatment_workup: Hepatitis B serology done: HBsAg and anti-HBc nonreactive (anti-HBs reactive from vaccination), so no HBV antiviral treatment is needed before rituximab; HCV and HIV nonreactive. Echo LVEF 60%, so anthracycline (doxorubicin in DA-EPOCH-R) is permitted. Renal and hepatic function normal. Bone marrow biopsy is not needed because PET-CT shows no marrow uptake. Outstanding before cycle 1: contrast MRI brain, lumbar puncture with CSF cytology and flow cytometry, sperm banking, G6PD level in case rasburicase is needed, and confirmation that the new port is functioning.
supportive_care: Tumor lysis syndrome (TLS) risk is intermediate: 12 cm mass, LDH about 3.6x ULN, uric acid 7.6 rising to 7.9 mg/dL, normal creatinine. Start allopurinol 300 mg daily 2-3 days before cycle 1 with oral/IV hydration and TLS labs (potassium, phosphate, calcium, uric acid, creatinine, LDH) every 12-24 hours for the first 72 hours; use rasburicase if uric acid keeps rising or creatinine increases (check G6PD first). G-CSF is mandatory with DA-EPOCH-R: filgrastim from day 6 until neutrophil recovery (or pegfilgrastim on day 6) every cycle, with twice-weekly CBCs to guide dose adjustment. DA-EPOCH-R is a 96-hour continuous infusion of vesicant drugs and needs central venous access: use the left chest port placed 2026-09-18, with an ambulatory infusion pump or inpatient administration. Offer sperm banking before cycle 1. Mediastinal mass with SVC narrowing: monitor closely during cycle 1 (consider an inpatient start), warn him to report worsening facial swelling, dyspnea, orthopnea, stridor or trouble swallowing liquids, and avoid sedation or general anesthesia without anesthetic review. PJP prevention per institutional DA-EPOCH-R practice, antiemetics, and a bowel regimen with vincristine. Continue CPAP for sleep apnea and albuterol as needed.
fitness_and_goals: Fit for intensive curative therapy: age 54, ECOG 1, LVEF 60%, normal renal and hepatic function, and no comorbidity that limits treatment (sleep apnea on CPAP, mild intermittent asthma and GERD do not). His goal is cure and he wants the most effective treatment; discuss the inpatient or pump-based infusion schedule, twice-weekly labs and time off work, since he hopes to keep working part time from home.

G6PD status in case rasburicase is needed
Clinical trial availability for MYC/BCL2-rearranged lymphoma
